predecessors.note: Home for Tswana speakers from 1961, self-governing from 1 June 1972; 'nominal independence on 6 December 1977', recognised only by South Africa and Transkei. The south-africa ledger records it as a vassal_start on the same day (its ledger 7).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: South Africa's Cliopatria shape (1976-1989, 2,060,667 km2) holds the homeland as plain South African land, and the 1990 shape (1,228,067 km2) is the 1990 anchor without any relation to Bophuthatswana. Infobox area 44,109 km2 in 1980; the four discs resolve to about 28,800 km2 (114 cells; ratio 0.65 to the infobox), which is within a factor of two (the pages name six or seven enclaves and give no outline; Mathanjana, north-east of Pretoria, is not placed because no page opened gives its coordinates). The gazetteer has no Bophuthatswana region (south-africa's ledger 7 and 14 name {region: Bophuthatswana}); a gap-filler may replace the discs with that region.

ledger.note: 6 December 1977: Bophuthatswana is declared 'independent' under Lucas Mangope; only South Africa and Transkei recognised it. 'nominal independence on 6 December 1977' (infobox); 'The Status of Bophuthatswana Act 89 of 1977 granted Bophuthatswana "independence" with effect from 6 December 1977' (Bantustan page). The pages name enclaves, not a boundary; the discs are the researcher's reading.

region.text: Mafeking, 'just outside the borders at independence'

ledger.note: 1980: Mafeking is incorporated after a local referendum ('Mafeking, just outside the borders at independence, was incorporated after a local referendum. It is now part of Mafikeng/Mmabatho'). Mafeking lies a few kilometres from Mmabatho, inside the same grid cell as the main enclave, so the map shows no change.

ledger.note: 27 April 1994: Bophuthatswana is reincorporated into South Africa. 'On 27 April 1994, it was reintegrated into South Africa with the coming into force of the country's interim constitution. Its territory was distributed between the new provinces of the Free State, Gauteng, Mpumalanga and North West Province.' The Bantustan page: 'their territories reincorporated into the Republic of South Africa with effect from 27 April 1994'; 'The dismantling of the homelands of Bophuthatswana and Ciskei was particularly difficult.'

ledger.note: 27 April 1994: the homeland ends after the March 1994 crisis (Mangope deposed on 12 March) and passes to the provinces of the new South Africa; infobox 'Dissolved: 27 April 1994', 'Succeeded by: South Africa'.

wars.name: 1988 Bophuthatswana coup attempt
wars.outcome: Coup of 10 February 1988 by Rocky Malebane-Metsing; South African Defence Force troops 'invaded and reinstated Mangope'. No change of land.
wars.note: The title is descriptive; the Bophuthatswana page is the only page opened. P. W. Botha said the South African government was 'opposed in principle to the obtaining or maintaining of power by violence'. A second coup attempt in 1990 followed protests.

wars.name: 1994 Bophuthatswana crisis
wars.outcome: 9-11 March 1994: Afrikaner right-wing groups mobilised at Mangope's invitation to Constand Viljoen, and AWB members shot at civilians near Mmabatho/Mafikeng and were repelled; on 12 March the South African government and the Transitional Executive Council deposed Mangope and appointed Tjaart van der Walt administrator; reincorporation followed on 27 April.
wars.note: No border moved before 27 April; the title is descriptive.

certainty.note: The homeland's limits were statutory (the Status of Bophuthatswana Act of 1977), so the edge is sharp; but the dossier draws the enclaves as discs because no page gives an outline, so the shape is approximate.

notes: Written by n-mod. NEIGHBOUR: south-africa ledger 7 (vassal_start 1977-12) and 14 (vassal_end 1994-04) use {region: Bophuthatswana}, which the gazetteer lacks (listed in the report); Transkei, Venda and Ciskei were said to have dossiers but no polities/ file with those slugs exists on the mount at this time. SPECS: four discs intersected with South Africa (the Mmabatho disc would otherwise reach Botswana); the main enclave's real extent (Mafikeng, Zeerust, Taung, Ganyesa and more) is not described by any page opened, so the 100 km disc is a reading. Mathanjana (north-east of Pretoria, later Mpumalanga) is named by the page but unplaced. Self-government from 1 June 1972 (infobox) precedes the dossier's start; the map draws the homeland as South African until independence. The 1990 South African shape (south-africa_1990, 1,228,067 km2) already loses the homelands, so the compile may need the vassal tint from the south-africa ledger and this dossier's land to agree.
